turns.assessment: The event was a brief, common impairment at t=600 rather than a persistent client failure: affected unprotected services accumulated two errored seconds, protected services switched and returned after 1.3 s. Stable power, OSNR, amplifier, and pump measurements argue strongly against a cut, loss increase, amplifier failure, or connector fault. A fast polarization transient on the shared aerial span fits the simultaneous errors without an optical-power alarm; the receiver-side error pattern favors the S23-to-S13 direction, E34.

proposals.rationale: E34 is the shared aerial fibre span in the S23-to-S13 direction. Wind or mechanical motion can cause a millisecond polarization excursion, producing the observed errored seconds and short protection switches while leaving OCM power, OSNR, and amplifier telemetry unchanged.
E18 is the reverse-direction fibre in the same aerial route and could have experienced the polarization transient, but the locations of the line-interface error observations favor E34.
Physical motion of the aerial span could instead have caused a very brief power excursion, although the complete absence of observed power changes makes a pure SOP transient more likely.
